title: Anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction)
summary: Use the person’s epinephrine immediately, call emergency services, and prevent sudden standing.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Anaphylaxis
actions: Use the person’s prescribed epinephrine auto-injector immediately. Follow the device instructions and inject into the middle of the outer thigh; many devices can be used through clothing.
Call emergency services at once. Do not wait to see whether epinephrine works.

Keep the person lying down and do not let them stand or walk. If breathing is harder when flat, allow a position that makes breathing easier with legs extended; in late pregnancy use the left side when possible.
If symptoms continue or return after 5 to 15 minutes and a second prescribed auto-injector is available, give it according to the device instructions or dispatcher guidance.
Monitor breathing and responsiveness. Use the recovery position if unresponsive but breathing normally; start CPR and use an AED if breathing is absent or abnormal.
prohibitions: Do not delay epinephrine while looking for an antihistamine.
Do not inject an auto-injector into a hand, finger, buttock, or lower leg.
Do not allow sudden standing or walking.
Do not leave the person alone after apparent improvement.

emergencyCall.text: Anaphylaxis is always an emergency, even if symptoms improve after epinephrine.
